source_quote: RHU offers a freshman program for students who have not earned a Lebanese
answer: The freshman program is for students who have not earned a Lebanese Baccalaureate or equivalent and bridges them to bachelor's eligibility. It has two tracks, Freshman Arts and Freshman Science, each of 30 credits that may be completed in two semesters.

source_quote: Freshman Arts 12 3 3 6 3 3
answer: Freshman Arts credit distribution: Humanities/Social Sciences 12, Math 3, Natural Sciences 3, Free Electives 6, English 3, Arabic 3 (30 credits).

source_quote: Freshman 6 6 9 3 3 3
answer: Freshman Sciences credit distribution: Humanities/Social Sciences 6, Math 6, Natural Sciences 9, Free Elective 3, English 3, Arabic 3 (30 credits).

source_quote: All students whose native language is Arabic must take an Arabic language course.
answer: All freshman students whose native language is Arabic must take an Arabic language course; students exempted from Arabic must take a substitute course to complete the 30 credits.

source_quote: A high school certificate based on 12 years of schooling, starting with Grade One,
answer: To join the Freshman Program, an applicant needs either a high school certificate based on 12 years of schooling starting from Grade One, recognized by the Lebanese MoEHE (fewer than 12 years is not recognized), or a GCE with at least five O-Level subjects and one A-Level or two AS-Level subjects, excluding languages.

source_quote: Freshman courses are identified by having a “1” as the first digit of the course
answer: Freshman courses are identified by a '1' as the first digit of the course number.

source_quote: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics* 3
answer: Freshman Arts, Fall (15 credits): BECN 190 Introduction to Economics, ENGL 101 Freshman English, MATH 189 Fundamentals of Algebra, a Free Elective, and a Humanities/Social Science Elective.

source_quote: * Required for application to the College of Business.
answer: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics is required in Freshman Arts for application to the College of Business.

source_quote: Natural Science Elective 3
answer: Freshman Arts, Spring (15 credits): ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, two Humanities/Social Science Electives, a Natural Science Elective, and a Free Elective.

source_quote: MATH 190 Calculus I 3
answer: Freshman Science, Fall (15 credits): ENGL 101 Freshman English, MATH 190 Calculus I, PHYS 190 General Physics I, Humanities/Social Science Elective I, and a Free Elective.

source_quote: MATH 191 Calculus II 3 MATH 190
answer: Freshman Science, Spring (15 credits): ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, MATH 191 Calculus II, PHYS 191 General Physics II, a Natural Science Elective, and Humanities/Social Science Elective II.

source_quote: This freshman-level course is designed for native speakers of Arabic to develop their
answer: ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, 3(3,0): a freshman course in Arabic for native speakers to develop reading and writing through essays and articles; it fulfills the freshman Arabic requirement and is mandatory for all native Arabic speakers.

source_quote: economic principles, issues, history, and institutions. It develops their economic literacy
answer: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics, 3(3,0): basic economic principles, issues, history and institutions, including markets, firms, economic systems, the role of government, capitalism, macroeconomic indicators, and supply and demand.

source_quote: focuses on the interrelatedness between reading and writing, whereby students
answer: ENGL 101 Freshman English, 3(3,0): develops reading and writing through rhetorical modes (classification, cause/effect, comparison/contrast), reviews grammar, and introduces research skills (evaluating sources, paraphrasing, summarizing, quoting) in APA style.

source_quote: Real number systems, radicals and rational exponents, polynomials, factoring,
answer: MATH 189 Fundamentals of Algebra, 3(3,0): real numbers, radicals and exponents, polynomials, factoring, fractional expressions, lines, functions and inverses, equations and inequalities, the fundamental theorem of algebra, and exponential and logarithmic functions.

source_quote: Functions and their graphs, limits and continuity, differentiation, applications of
answer: MATH 190 Calculus I, 3(3,0): functions and graphs, limits and continuity, differentiation and its applications, extreme values and the mean value theorem, definite and indefinite integrals, and substitution.

source_quote: Covers limits and indeterminate forms with L’Hôpital’s Rule, optimization,
answer: MATH 191 Calculus II, 3(3,0): indeterminate forms and L'Hôpital's Rule, optimization, antiderivatives, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, areas, volumes, arc length, surfaces of revolution, and parametric and vector functions.

source_quote: curvature, and normal vectors. Prerequisite: Math
answer: The prerequisite for MATH 191 Calculus II is MATH 190.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and principles of Mechanics:
answer: PHYS 190 General Physics - Mechanics, 3(3,0): vectors, displacement, velocity, acceleration, 1D and projectile motion, forces, Newton's laws, work, energy, momentum, collisions, torque, and rotational motion.

source_quote: This course is an introduction to electricity and magnetism. In this course, students will
answer: PHYS 191 General Physics - Electricity and Magnetism, 3(3,0): electric charges, forces and fields, potential, capacitance, DC circuits, magnetic force and field, induction, AC circuits, and electromagnetic waves.

source_quote: inductance, alternating-current circuits, and electromagnetic waves. Prerequisite:
answer: The prerequisite for PHYS 191 General Physics - Electricity and Magnetism is PHYS 190.

source_quote: Students in this course will learn the basic concepts and techniques of accounting,
answer: BACC 150 Introduction to Accounting, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic accounting concepts and techniques, including accounting information systems, costing, estimation, and management accounting.

source_quote: This course covers the basic tenets of the legal system and how they may apply to
answer: BADM 155 Introduction to Law, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic tenets of the legal system and how they apply to business sectors.

source_quote: This is an introductory course to the fundamental principles of biology that covers the
answer: BIOL 102 Introduction to Biology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the chemical basis of life, cell structure and function, genetics, and human body systems.

source_quote: A freshman-level course that introduces students to the basic concepts of genetics,
answer: BIOL 170 Basic Concepts in Biology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: genetics, evolution, ecology, and the forms and functions of plants and animals.

source_quote: This course provides a general overview of management basics, including principles
answer: BMGT 150 Basics of Management, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: overview of management basics, including management science principles and buying and selling.

source_quote: Students will learn the basics of different aspects of hospitality, such as food, lodging,
answer: BMGT 155 Introduction to Hospitality Management, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: hospitality basics (food, lodging, beverages, pastries) and hotel, restaurant and resort operations.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the nature of business, the types of commercial
answer: BMKT 150 Introduction to Business and Commerce, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the nature of business, types of commercial activities, market analysis, and their interrelationships.

source_quote: This course introduces students to fundamental programming concepts such as
answer: CCEE 111 Computer Programming, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: variables, loops, conditional statements, event handling, and using math and code to think creatively.

source_quote: This course covers issues related to the development and implementation of internet-
answer: CCEE 112 Internet Development and Support, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: Internet organization, site registration, e-mail and Web servers, Web page development, legal issues, firewalls, TCP/IP, FTP, and gateways.

source_quote: This course is designed to help students understand the basic functions of a computer
answer: CCEE 121 Computer Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic computer functions, operating systems, word processing, spreadsheets, databases, presentation graphics, and the internet.

source_quote: This course introduces the technical aspects of computer hardware units. Topics
answer: CCEE 122 Computer Hardware, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: technical aspects of hardware units, computer organization, and internal and external communication.

source_quote: In this course, students will learn how to set up a computer, diagnose simple faults,
answer: CCEE 123 Introduction to Computer Troubleshooting, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: setting up a computer and diagnosing and troubleshooting simple faults.

source_quote: In this course, the students will be introduced to the technologies involved in the Audio
answer: CCEE 131 Introduction to Audio-Visual Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: audio and video communication technologies including video production, multimedia, sound, animation, and photography.

source_quote: This course includes the public switched telephone network; the telephone and the
answer: CCEE 141 Switching Systems Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the public switched telephone network, local loop, inter-exchange signaling, evolution of switching, traffic statistics, and space/time-division switching.

source_quote: This course covers analog and digital communication systems: basic principles of
answer: CCEE 142 Basics of Analog and Digital Communications, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: telecommunication principles, transducers, and modulation and demodulation.

source_quote: Students study the principles and methods of chemistry, including atomic structure,
answer: CHEM 160 Chemistry I, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of chemistry including atomic structure, periodic trends, and naming inorganic and organic formulas.

source_quote: Students learn about acids, bases, and chemical equilibria; the groups in the periodic
answer: CHEM 170 Chemistry II, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: acids, bases, chemical equilibria, periodic table groups, and surveys of organic and nuclear chemistry.

source_quote: The study of architectural technology from the Greek civilization to the present
answer: CIVE 105 History of Architectural Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: architectural technology from Greek civilization to the present, structural systems, materials, and socio-economic influences on design.

source_quote: The study of stress and strain, deformation, simplified analysis of torsion, shear, and
answer: CIVE 120 Introductory Strength of Materials, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: stress and strain, torsion, shear, beam stresses, design and deflection, columns, and materials testing.

source_quote: Emphasis is placed on applying structural design principles for new and existing
answer: CIVE 121 Concrete Construction Methods and Concrete Structures, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: structural design principles for concrete structures, concrete and masonry, shallow foundations, and renovation issues.

source_quote: Review of water distribution plumbing and related fundamentals. This course covers
answer: CIVE 135 Plumbing and Air Conditioning, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: water distribution plumbing, piping, valves, backflow prevention, water quality, hydraulics, and air-conditioning fundamentals.

source_quote: A study of topographic surveying and mapping. Determination of land areas,
answer: CIVE 140 Introduction to Surveying, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: topographic surveying and mapping, land areas, construction, control and boundary surveys, route and street layout, and surveying instruments.

source_quote: Measurement and graphic description of topography, topometric descriptions of
answer: CIVE 141 Fundamentals of Topometry, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: measurement and graphic description of topography using mapping techniques.

source_quote: Principles and techniques of vertical aerial photograph photogrammetry, distance,
answer: CIVE 142 Photogrammetry, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: vertical aerial photograph photogrammetry, distance, direction, area and scale calculations and interpretation.

source_quote: A horizontal and vertical datum, gravitation and centrifugal forces; measurements of
answer: CIVE 143 Geodesy, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: horizontal and vertical datums, gravity measurement and reduction, geoid and ellipsoid, deflection of the vertical, and orthometric and dynamic heights.

source_quote: Topographic mapping, spatial analysis, map production and cartography, spatial
answer: CIVE 144 Mapping, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: topographic mapping, spatial analysis, cartography, reference systems, scale, projections, generalization, and symbolization.

source_quote: Surface processes and landforms; their implications for land use and for present, past,
answer: CIVE 145 Geomorphology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: surface processes and landforms, weathering, glacial and fluvial processes, mass wasting, and tectonic controls.

source_quote: Construction and surveying regulations and laws in Lebanon and their applications to
answer: CIVE 146 Construction and Surveying Regulations and Laws, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: Lebanese construction and surveying laws applied to land use, urban development, and buildings, including the law of practice and professional registration.

source_quote: This course introduces students to construction, alteration, repair, or improvement on
answer: CIVE 148 Introduction to Public Works, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: state-funded construction and repair on public land and the administration and supervision of public works.

source_quote: This course covers the three monotheistic religions. It compares the idea of God and
answer: CVLN 160 Monotheistic Religions: A Comparative Study, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: compares the idea of God and the law in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

source_quote: This course reviews the history of the Arabs from the pagan days through the twentieth
answer: CVLN 161 The Arabs, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: history of the Arabs from pagan times through the twentieth century.

source_quote: A literary attempt to understand the universe's origins as found in texts from various
answer: CVLN 170 God and Creation: East and West, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: a literary look at the origins of the universe in texts from world cultures.

source_quote: An introduction to the themes and challenges of autonomy and independence as
answer: CVLN 180 Youth and the Growing Up Process, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: themes of autonomy and independence in youth, studied through major literary works.
